Yeast Ykt6p Trafficking Pathways: An Evidence-Based Reassessment
TL;DR

The textbook claim that yeast Ykt6p is "essential for ER-to-Golgi transport" is an overinterpretation of a 1997 depletion phenotype. The bona fide ER→Golgi R-SNARE in wild-type yeast is Sec22p; Ykt6p only substitutes for Sec22p when Sec22p is absent (Liu & Barlowe 2002), and Ykt6 depletion blocks the ER-Golgi step largely as an indirect/secondary consequence of its essential intra-Golgi function (Gao, Reggiori & Ungermann, JCB 2018). [Molecular Biology of the Cell](https://www.molbiolcell.org/doi/10.1091/mbc.e02-04-0204)
The best-supported direct functions of yeast Ykt6p are intra-Golgi/retrograde Golgi transport (in the fusogenic Sed5–Gos1–Ykt6 + Sft1 SNAREpin; Parlati et al. PNAS 2002), biosynthetic Golgi→vacuole transport via the CPY, ALP and Cvt pathways (Kweon, Rothe, Conibear & Stevens, MBoC 2003), endosome/PVC traffic (Dilcher et al. JBC 2001), and autophagosome–vacuole fusion as the autophagosomal R-SNARE (Bas et al. JCB 2018; Gao et al. JCB 2018).
In homotypic vacuole fusion, Ykt6p does NOT zipper into the fusogenic trans-SNARE bundle (which is Vam3/Vti1/Vam7 + Nyv1); instead it acts upstream as a palmitoyl-CoA donor that palmitoylates Vac8 via its N-terminal longin domain (Dietrich et al. EMBO J 2004; EMBO Reports 2005). A 2024 yeast paper (Watanabe et al., JBC) shows Ykt6 can substitute for Nyv1 in the vacuolar R-SNARE slot only when forced, confirming Nyv1 as the primary in vivo R-SNARE. [PubMed Central](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC1299260/)
